decisive_items: continuous anterior chest pain exacerbated by deep breathing
slightly increased global T1 and T2 mapping values, minimal hyperintensity of pericardium without effusion
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin: 128.00 pg/ml initially, peaked at 142.00 pg/ml
response.rationale: Myopericarditis best explains concurrent myocardial injury (elevated troponin, increased T1/T2 mapping) and pericardial inflammation (pleuritic chest pain, pericardial hyperintensity, PR-segment changes). Pericarditis alone misses the myocardial component; Lyme carditis lacks typical erythema migrans and tick exposure; ACS is excluded by normal coronary CT angiography.

rejected.why: Explains pericardial chest pain and MRI findings but does not account for elevated troponin and myocardial T1/T2 changes.
AV block is present, but the genital vesicular/umbilicated lesions are not erythema migrans and there is no tick exposure history.
Elevated troponin and ECG changes are nonspecific, and normal coronary CT angiography excludes obstructive coronary disease.
